# JCLAW_LESSONS — the merged ledger

**Generated by `scripts/research/mergeLessons.py` from the 8 study files in `docs/research/runs/jclaw-2026-09-14/`. Do not hand-edit — edit the studies or the cluster map and re-run.**

52 candidates in, 52 out: 36 in 8 clusters, 16 skipped with a reason. The script raises rather than emitting a ledger with a dropped id.

Ranking rule, from the kickoff: *this defect class has already bitten us* > *could* > speculative, then cheapness. Clusters are listed in that order.

## Clusters

### C1 — A zero nobody proved could be non-zero

*Has it bitten us?* Has bitten us TWICE: claimcheck's first version reported `0 failures` over four verified wrong cites (closing it raised 82), and the Node 26 spec reporter hid 3 chaos results from a probe whose grep no longer matched (memory `feedback-probe-parser-must-match`).

**7 candidates · 2 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-instructions-4` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | Validate a measuring harness against a known-zero before believing a number it produces |
| `hooks-ci-sandbox-4` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | A fail-open branch carries its reason on the line, and never hides a measurement |
| `harness-evolution-2` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | A detector must be shown capable of matching before a zero from it is reported |
| `architecture-rules-2` | HAVE | **SKIP** | A live-match FLOOR beside every scan that could match nothing, plus a sanity probe that the scan is reading the right corpus — so a predicate that silently stops matching cannot pass vacuously (and a frozen store cannot be pruned to empty on a regeneration run). |
| `evals-ruler-5` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | Validate the harness against a known-zero AND a known-one before trusting it, and pin that a scan 'scanned at all' — an absence-assertion over an empty set passes vacuously. |
| `gate-guards-4` | GAP | **ADAPT** | The harness repo's own test command must fail on zero tests and pin a floor — `node --test <glob>` passes when the glob matches nothing |
| `gate-guards-2` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | A skip-guarded suite must fail, not skip, when the thing it is guarded on is present but the guard's own probe drifted — 'a checker switched off' must go red |

### C2 — A written claim that quietly stopped being true

*Has it bitten us?* Live in the tree right now: `CLAUDE.md:67` has named `.claude/ship-bar.md` since commit 995bb52 deleted that file on 2026-09-08. JClaw hit the same class harder — 0dfcd451 corrected six contradicted AGENTS.md claims at once.

**4 candidates · 2 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-instructions-1` | GAP | **ADOPT** | Mechanically resolve every repo path an always-loaded instruction file names; fail when one does not exist |
| `agent-instructions-2` | GAP | **SKIP** | Stamp a generated instruction block with the date and commit it was verified against |
| `architecture-rules-6` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | A rule the docs admit is review-only becomes a test with a named, reasoned, stale-checked exception list — the FreezingArchRule move applied to our config-label rule. |
| `harness-evolution-1` | GAP | **ADOPT** | Instruction-file rot is a recurring defect with a measurable cost, not a tidiness issue |

### C3 — The guard on the guard can be switched off or fooled

*Has it bitten us?* Live hole: `tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73` reads the runner's plant count with an unanchored regex a comment satisfies. JClaw shipped the same bug and closed it in 88b142ee.

**7 candidates · 2 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `architecture-rules-3` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Gate-conformance test: a test that reads the gate's OWN configuration (build file, hook, compiler flags), strips comments first, and fails on the known ways of switching the gate off or downgrading it — so disarming a gate is itself a red test, not a later discovery. |
| `gate-guards-1` | GAP | **ADOPT** | Fail the suite on a focused test (`it.only` / `describe.only`) in every environment, not only under CI |
| `gate-guards-3` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Every file that declares tests must be one the runner collects — compare the runner's discovery against the tree, with a floor so an empty scan cannot pass |
| `gate-guards-5` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Gate-wiring conformance: a test that reads the hook and the checker configs with comments stripped and asserts the gate is wired, on, and at error severity — including that git is actually pointed at the hook |
| `gate-guards-7` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | Two copies of one gate rule are pinned equal or collapsed to one — schema/enum drift between the thing that documents and the thing that enforces fails a test |
| `harness-evolution-3` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | A gate that reads a config or source file by raw substring passes when the line it guards is commented out |
| `hooks-ci-sandbox-5` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Detect that the hook path is not wired, and say so |

### C4 — A fan-out that cannot tell dead from empty, or stop

*Has it bitten us?* The most expensive class we have: round 1 spawned 28 agents, lost 25 to a wall, burned 1,369,556 tokens and verified 0 lessons. Memory `feedback-fail-closed-agent-accounting` and `feedback-cap-foreign-repo-fanout` are both scars from it.

**7 candidates · 4 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resilience-gates-1` | GAP | **ADOPT** | Consecutive-failure streak breaker: after N agent deaths in a row, stop spawning and report the unspawned work as NOT_SPAWNED (fail-closed), rather than letting every queued agent launch into a dead dependency. |
| `resilience-gates-2` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | Reason-carrying failure: every breaker transition and every refusal carries WHY (Reason enum with a `manual()` split; ManuallyIsolated vs BreakerOpen), so an operator's stop is never read as the dependency breaking and a diagnosis can be made from the record alone. |
| `resilience-gates-3` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | Half-open probe: after a trip, admit a bounded number of probes and re-open on the first that fails; close only when all succeed — never relaunch the whole fleet on hope. |
| `subagent-lifecycle-1` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Orphan-process sweep by command-line signature: list candidates, EXCLUDE live ones explicitly, SIGTERM, wait, escalate to SIGKILL, and kill the whole tree (descendants snapshotted before the parent dies). |
| `subagent-lifecycle-2` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | Every spawned run carries an absolute ceiling set by the OPERATOR, not by the run itself, independent of activity — on top of any activity-based budget. |
| `subagent-lifecycle-3` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | Breadth cap enforced at spawn time for the WHOLE fan-out: refuse before anything is created when running + requested exceeds the cap, with a message naming the numbers. |
| `subagent-lifecycle-4` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | In-flight markers are reconciled by AGE, not trusted: anything still marked RUNNING after a restart and older than a grace window is stamped DEAD with a distinct reason; a marker younger than the grace window is left alone. |

### C5 — The gate measures a different artifact than the one that ships

*Has it bitten us?* Unmeasured here. `.githooks/pre-commit` runs typecheck/vitest/lint against the WORKING TREE while committing the INDEX; no partial-commit defect is on record.

**2 candidates · 0 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate-guards-6` | GAP | **ADAPT** | The gate's input must be the artifact being committed: refuse a partially staged commit rather than test the working tree and stamp the index |
| `hooks-ci-sandbox-1` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Gate the staged tree, not the working tree — read staged blobs with `git show :<path>` |

### C6 — The ruler's own content is unpinned

*Has it bitten us?* Adjacent to a fixed bug: our fan-out accounting was fail-open twice. The ruler here is `measure-refute.js` / `measure-verify.js`, whose lens set and schema nothing fingerprints.

**5 candidates · 2 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evals-ruler-2` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | A COMPUTED fingerprint of the ruler's content (ids, inputs, check kinds/args/limits, required tools — prose excluded) is stamped on every recording and every report; scoring or comparing across a fingerprint change prints a warning BEFORE any result, and the computed hash replaced a hand-bumped version number that 'protected against the author who remembered to bump'. |
| `evals-ruler-4` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | Calibration declared by the suite and applied at run time: `requiredTools` lives in the suite file; capture grants EXACTLY those to the dedicated eval agent, revokes everything else, clears the state the previous sweep's tools left behind, refuses to touch any non-eval agent, and the tool gate is enforced at EXECUTION (ToolRegistry.execute), not only in the tool list shown to the model. |
| `evals-ruler-6` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | The loader REJECTS what the scorer does not implement rather than ignoring it: unknown keys at every level, unknown check kinds, wrong arity per kind, JSON-Schema keywords the validator does not enforce — because "a hand-rolled subset that ignored the keywords it does not understand would report passes it never checked". |
| `evals-ruler-7` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | Assert what HAPPENED, not what was asked: `tool_result_includes` scores the tool's returned text (a case passed green while its web_fetch returned HTTP 404), and `toolsCalled` (dispatched) is split from `toolsAttempted` (emitted) so refused/invented calls never score as work done. |
| `resilience-gates-4` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | Deterministic, in-process tool-result verification with a structural post-condition: a result that is EMPTY, error-prefixed, or fails the tool's own post-condition is not a pass, and SKIPPED is 'not a pass — an absence of one'. Free checks first, no critic model. |

### C7 — Seams: one clock, one RNG, one copy of a rule

*Has it bitten us?* Largely already ours — `src/core/` is RNG-seamed by contract and `tests/config-purity.test.ts` enforces zero numeric literals. Kept as a cluster so the claims are checkable, not because a gap is assumed.

**3 candidates · 1 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `architecture-rules-1` | PARTIAL | **ADAPT** | Frozen violation store with BOTH switches pinned off: a listed exception that stops matching FAILS until its line is deleted by hand, so the store can only shrink deliberately and never holds ghost entries. |
| `architecture-rules-4` | PARTIAL | **ADOPT** | One clock seam and one randomness seam, enforced by a scan of ACCESSES (not by prose): every wall-clock or ambient-random read outside the seam fails the build; the rule text lives in the test, and known limitations are asserted as tests rather than stated in comments. |
| `architecture-rules-5` | GAP | **ADAPT** | Property-style tests for invariants that are easier to state than to enumerate — round trip, idempotence, a bound that holds for every input, an order that survives — with `tries` pinned, the wall-time budget written beside it, and the generated input carried in every failure message. |

### C8 — An action gate sitting between the model and the tool

*Has it bitten us?* Already ours in one form: the global `PreToolUse` hook `~/.claude/hooks/launch-gate-guard.py` denies a deploy while the launch gate is red.

**1 candidates · 1 ADOPT**

| id | our state | verdict | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resilience-gates-5` | GAP | **ADOPT** | Dangerous-action gate as CODE between the model and the tool: fail closed on unknown origin, standing grants keyed narrowly and revocable, the refusal text tells the model 'do not retry this action'. |

## Skipped — every id, with the reason it is not worth building

| id | our state | reason |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-instructions-3` | PARTIAL | We already hold the settled verdicts (OWNER_PERMISSION_RULING, REBUILD_READINESS, the CLAUDE.md invariants block); a `docs/spikes/` folder would be a third home for the same facts — state-schema drift for no gain. |
| `agent-instructions-5` | GAP | The comment delete test is a judgement rule no gate can check, priced in per-turn tokens forever, and our actual comment problem is the opposite: the gate scripts' comments carry load-bearing defect history. |
| `architecture-rules-7` | HAVE | Structured-concurrency scope semantics — we have no concurrency in `src/core/` (fixed 60 Hz single-threaded Sim) and no threads to cancel. |
| `evals-ruler-1` | HAVE | ERRORED-is-not-FAILED is already implemented in `measure-refute.js`'s fail-closed accounting (a dead run returns `fatalCount: null`, never 0). |
| `evals-ruler-3` | HAVE | Baseline regression compare — `tests/duel-baseline.test.ts` already pins the behavioural baseline, and a second compare layer over research runs has no consumer. |
| `evals-ruler-8` | HAVE | Per-case model-call budgets assume a runtime we do not have; our budget control is the session limit and the breadth cap (C4). |
| `harness-evolution-4` | HAVE | Classify-before-naming-a-cause: our `run_step` names only the failing step and prints the tool's own output, so it cannot assert a wrong cause. |
| `harness-evolution-5` | HAVE | Ship the measurement in the commit body — already a standing rule (ship-bar rule 3) that this repo's history follows. |
| `hooks-ci-sandbox-2` | HAVE | The `grep -q` + `pipefail` SIGPIPE trap: our hook is `#!/bin/sh` with neither setting, and the one script that does carry `set -euo pipefail` uses no `grep -q`. Nothing to make red. |
| `hooks-ci-sandbox-3` | HAVE | Duplicate of harness-evolution-4. |
| `hooks-ci-sandbox-6` | HAVE | We spawn no harness subprocess of our own, so there is no argv to wrap in `sandbox-exec`. |
| `resilience-gates-6` | GAP | Model/provider failover assumes we own the LLM call; we do not. |
| `resilience-gates-7` | HAVE | Compaction and tool-result stubbing are the harness's job, not ours, and Claude Code already does both. |
| `subagent-lifecycle-5` | GAP | A cooperative stop flag the child carries needs a child process we control; our subagents are the harness's. |
| `subagent-lifecycle-6` | HAVE | Single-settle terminal state — `measure-refute.js` already writes each verdict once, to disk, before returning. |
| `subagent-lifecycle-7` | HAVE | Surfacing a timed-out child's partial output is exactly the salvage rule we already run (agents write JSON to disk before returning; 5 of 8 round-1 studies survived because of it). |
